svg.title: Four routes out of one repository, and the one column the registry owns
svg.desc: One repository box on the left sends a single vertical spine to four numbered rows, each drawn as the same three boxes at the same widths. Route one is a package on PyPI, npm or a container image, then an MCP Registry entry describing it, then the user's host resolving and running it with uvx. Route two is a deployment you operate, then a registry entry carrying a remote URL, then the host simply connecting with nothing installed locally. Route three is a release asset ending in .mcpb, then an optional registry entry carrying a file hash, then the user double-clicking it and the installer asking for the declared user configuration. Route four is the baseline, drawn in the same three boxes but greyed: a git clone, a configuration file edited by hand with one absolute path in it, and a server that runs for one person and reaches nobody else. A dashed band sits behind the middle column only, spanning the first three rows and stopping above the fourth, labelled as everything the registry ever stores, with a note that route four never touches it. Three chips along the bottom carry the caveats that apply to every route through the registry: it is in preview rather than generally available and may reset its data, consumers should assume minimal-to-no moderation so a listing is not a safety signal, and nothing can ever be unpublished, only given a different status.
svg.text: Four routes out, and what the registry actually stores
It stores metadata about three of them. It hosts the code for none of them.
the host resolves and runs it
Three caveats on every route that goes through the registry
a listing is not a safety signal
only a status you can change
